items.notes: CBS framed it as no decisions at all; UN News and Down To Earth say only the cover text failed. Cross-check: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/un-cop31-climate-conference-ends-no-agreement-fossil-fuel-debate-standstill/
items.text: [[e:COP31|2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] closed in Antalya on 22 Nov after two days of overtime without adopting its cover decision. COP31 President [[p:Murat Kurum]] said there was no agreement on the text after the EU formally objected to a draft without fossil-fuel language, joined by Panama and the Marshall Islands. Narrower decisions did pass, including the Just Transition Work Programme and an adaptation-finance road map. [[p:António Guterres]] called the outcome deeply disappointing; COP32 goes to Addis Ababa.

items.notes: Vessel and forces unidentified; link to a Kharg blockade-runner is Euronews's inference. IRGC mine claim may repeat a 20 Nov claim. Gulf News cites an analyst saying the US hit a tanker; CENTCOM silent. JMIC counts seven tankers hit near Hormuz since 16 Nov.
items.text: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on the evening of 22 Nov that a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, close to the US blockade line, amid reports that an Iranian tanker had left Kharg to test the [[e:2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis|blockade]]. Neither Washington nor Tehran confirmed a US strike. The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] claims two 'violating' supertankers hit mines east of the strait and that it downed a US drone. [[p:Donald Trump]] told Fox News blockade-runners would end up at the bottom of the sea.

items.notes: Neither side's claims independently verified. Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks have killed 26 in the kingdom since September.
items.text: The [[p:Houthis]] say they scored a direct hit on Saudi Arabia's [[p:Petro Rabigh]] refinery north of Jeddah and struck a radar in Wadi ad-Dawasir. The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a drone heading for Riyadh and a missile, with no damage, and has not confirmed a refinery hit. Houthi media say Saudi strikes wounded six at a Sanaa fuel station and killed four in Hodeidah.

items.notes: FT original paywalled, not read; anonymous sourcing.
items.text: The Trump administration has told European and Ukrainian officials it wants a Russia–Ukraine settlement before Democrats take control of Congress in January, the Financial Times reports, citing four people briefed. Envoys [[p:Steve Witkoff]] and [[p:Jared Kushner]] reportedly set out the timeline in Moscow, Dublin and Berlin. Ukrainian officials are said to fear pressure to accept terms favouring Moscow; the White House did not comment.

items.notes: Zelenskyy wants an all-for-all prisoner exchange from the next round (Kyiv Post, 22 Nov). Peskov quote via RIA Novosti.
items.text: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says the US proposed in Berlin that the next Ukraine–Europe–US–Russia round take place before Christmas, and he agreed; security advisers will first meet to set the agenda. Kremlin spokesman [[p:Dmitry Peskov]] said the meeting will happen soon but dates are uncertain. Zelenskyy also floated a three-way leaders' meeting at the G20 in Miami on 14–15 Dec, though Kyiv has no invitation.

Kremlin aide [[p:Yuri Ushakov]] invited the national security advisers of France, Germany and the UK to Moscow for talks on ending the war, RFE/RL reports; no decision has been made. Berlin repeated that it is ready to talk to Russia, while a French adviser said Europe would join only if Moscow accepts its full role in the wider talks, not separate bilateral tracks.

items.notes: Putin refusal also in Meduza (Russian). ISW (analysis) says such truces are workable only along the Dnipro line.
items.text: Zelenskyy published a list of 15 occupied settlements on the Dnipro's left bank in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts where Kyiv proposes local ceasefires to evacuate civilians. [[p:Vladimir Putin]] said on 19 Nov that Russia would not negotiate local ceasefires after the Crimean Bridge strikes. [[p:Donald Trump]] nonetheless told Fox News Washington is working on a larger-scale ceasefire.

Foreign Minister [[p:Sergey Lavrov]] said in a Channel One documentary that south-eastern and central Ukraine, including Kyiv, are traditionally Russian lands. [[p:Institute for the Study of War|ISW]] says such statements conflict with the US proposals reportedly on the table.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Strike confirmed; sinking and method are Ukrainian claims. Casualties disputed (Meduza headline says Russians and Libyans killed; UNITED24 says none). Russia silent at time of logging. UNITED24: https://united24media.com/world/ukraine-sinks-russian-corvette-1000-miles-from-home-in-stunning-seven-drone-operation-off-libya-24608
items.text: A large explosion destroyed a Russian warship refuelling at Benghazi naval base, provisionally identified by Naval News as the Project 20380 corvette Merkury. On 23 Nov the [[p:Security Service of Ukraine|SBU]] claimed the operation and Zelenskyy confirmed it: the SBU says seven sea drones launched from a 'mother ship' sank the corvette and hit the sanctioned cargo ship Angara. Eastern Libya's government condemned a breach of sovereignty and opened a joint investigation with Russia.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Fires confirmed; extent of damage reported only. Afipsky and Ilsky refineries were hit on 18 Nov.
items.text: Drones set fire to [[p:Lukoil]]'s Perm refinery about 1,500 km from the front; the governor acknowledged damage to an unnamed industrial facility. The Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov and the Kaleykino pumping station in Tatarstan, start of the [[p:Druzhba pipeline]], were also hit overnight, per geolocated footage and the Rostov governor. Ukraine's General Staff says at least nine refineries have been hit since late October.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.text: Deputy PM [[p:Alexander Novak]] told oil companies to produce more gasoline below the Euro-5 standard, keep importing and speed up repairs after Ukrainian strikes. The Moscow Times cites estimates that at least 13 plants have been hit since late October and that refining is about a third below pre-war levels.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Weapon unclear (Meduza, RBC-Ukraine: a drone). Two people reported missing.
items.text: A Russian strike partly collapsed a five-storey apartment block in Dymer, north of Kyiv, killing 11, the regional governor said on 23 Nov; a seven-year-old was pulled out alive after about 14 hours. Zelenskyy said Russia used about 2,700 drones, 1,460 glide bombs and 165 missiles in a week and called US delays in approving already-paid Patriot interceptors hard to understand.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.text: A strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two, including a child, and injured 58, according to Zelenskyy; Russia says it hit the city's power plant. Ukraine reports intercepting Russia's new small Filin cruise missile over Chernihiv oblast, and a missile again hit the Pechenihy reservoir dam in Kharkiv oblast.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: ISW assessments are analysis; General Staff figures are combatant claims. Russia claims Sosnovyi Bir (Kharkiv oblast), unverified.
items.text: ISW reports a Russian infiltration into northern Kostiantynivka, mixed movement around Dobropillia, Russian gains north-east of Kupiansk and Lyman, and no Russian gains near Huliaipole, where Ukraine counterattacked. The General Staff counted 17 assaults towards Kostiantynivka and 15 towards Pokrovsk by the morning of 23 Nov. Defence Minister Khmara says Crimean Bridge repairs could take months to a year; Russia says rail traffic has resumed.

items.notes: State-owned outlet; Meduza cross-check. Answers W-261109-05.
items.text: The [[p:State Duma]] passed the 2027–29 budget in second reading by 383 votes to none. It plans 48.74 trillion roubles of spending against 43.3 trillion of revenue in 2027, a 5.4 trillion deficit, and raises the veterans' fund to 70 billion roubles. The third reading is set for 24 Nov.

The Duma passed in first reading bills raising fines for spreading 'extremist materials' to 50,000–100,000 roubles and introducing fines of up to 1 million roubles for 'discrediting traditional values', plus a bill raising women's maximum military service age to 50. It also passed a law restricting library access to books by 'foreign agents'.

The Justice Ministry added 13 exiles sentenced in absentia, among them [[p:Lyubov Sobol]], [[p:Maxim Katz]] and [[p:Pyotr Verzilov]], to its list of people barred from renewing passports, using consular services or managing property in Russia. Critics call it a 'civil death' law (translated); the list now has 35 names.

Finance committee MP [[p:Yaroslav Zhelezniak]] says Ukraine's 2027 budget will not come up in the 23–26 Nov plenary week because it still needs coordination with the IMF and other partners; he expects final adoption on 7–10 Dec, after an original target of 20 Nov.

[[p:National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine|NABU]] and prosecutors charged the head of an SBU unit with leaking plans of an Ukrnafta investigation in exchange for gifts, including a ski-resort stay and use of a BMW. On 17 Nov NABU charged four people over an alleged €1.1m bribe to fabricate a criminal case.
